title: Trust Accounting Rule — Meeting Closing Fees from Trust on Contingency Placement Agreements
content:
**Rule.** When a creditor client with a termination notice on record settles the fees it owes on an agreement under the Contingency Placement Agreements, part of the fees owed may first be met from the collections Ridgeline holds in trust for the client, and how depends on the remittance terms:

- on a net-remittance agreement, the available trust balance is set against the whole of the fees owed;
- on a gross-remittance agreement whose tier allows fees to be offset against remittance, the available trust balance is set against the open invoiced fees, whether or not they are past due, and never against more than those open invoiced fees;
- on any other agreement nothing is met from trust, and the whole fees owed are paid.

**Defined amounts.**

- *Open invoiced fees* are the fee invoices booked on the agreement less every fee payment and every fee credit booked on it, and never less than zero.
- *Trust balance held* is the consumer collections Ridgeline holds in its trust account for the client on the agreement and has not yet remitted — collections booked less reversals, retained fees and remittances.
- *Available trust balance* is the trust balance held on the agreement less the reserves held back against it on the day of the payment, and never less than zero.
- *Amount met from trust* is the lesser of the available trust balance and the fees owed on a net-remittance agreement; the lesser of the available trust balance and the open invoiced fees on a gross-remittance agreement whose tier allows the offset; and nothing otherwise.

**Effect on the payment.** The amount met from trust is taken off the agreement's fees owed itself; every amount taken off the payment is taken off that same fees owed, the payment is never less than zero, and it is rounded to the cent once at the end. The amount met from trust is settled from the trust balance when the closing statement is drawn.

The remittance basis is read from the agreement record; whether the tier allows the offset is the tier's offset figure.

## Hypothetical cases

Inputs: fees owed 3000.00 USD; fee invoices booked 2600.00 USD, fee payments 900.00 USD and fee credits 100.00 USD, so open invoiced fees are 1600.00 USD; trust balance held 2200.00 USD with nothing held back, so the available trust balance is 2200.00 USD.

| Remittance terms | Amount met from trust | Remaining fees owed before anything else is taken off |
|---|---|---|
| Net remittance | lesser of 2200.00 and 3000.00: 2200.00 USD | 800.00 USD |
| Gross remittance, tier allows offset | lesser of 2200.00 and 1600.00: 1600.00 USD | 1400.00 USD |
| Gross remittance, tier does not allow offset | nothing | 3000.00 USD |

With invoices booked of 900.00 USD against payments and credits of 1000.00 USD, the open invoiced fees are zero, not a negative figure, and a gross-remittance agreement meets nothing from trust.
